key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled solver combines near-wall and bulk transport models to support inverse modeling of thin boundary layers, with agentic AI guiding optimization.
engineering_relevance: The framework can reduce mesh requirements and computational cost for high-Péclet transport while enforcing governing equations and boundary conditions as hard constraints.
method: Discretize perturbation-based inner and outer transport equations with finite elements.
Couple overlapping domains through differentiable Schwarz iterations that enforce interface continuity.
Use adjoint sensitivities for optimization, with an AI agent staging optimization and expanding an admissible functional basis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reduced computational cost versus a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI advantage for functional-basis unknowns than for high-dimensional nodal fields, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Agentic optimization benefits appear representation-dependent; performance on high-dimensional nodal unknowns requires careful validation.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
